title: Branch-variable selection returns a free variable
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables and $\rho$ a restriction. Suppose that at least one term of $f$ is not killed by $\rho$, and that no term of $f$ is fixed by $\rho$. Then the branch-variable selection procedure applied to $f$ and $\rho$ succeeds, returning a variable $v$ that is free in $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: some term of f is not killed by ρ (¬∀ t∈f, killedBy)
no term of f is fixed by ρ (¬∃ t∈f, fixedBy)
replaced:
When not every term of $f$ is killed by $\rho$ and no term is fixed by $\rho$, the function
$\mathrm{selectBranchVar}\,f\,\rho$ returns some variable $v$, and that $v$ is free in $\rho$.
